chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Mahziyar who said:

A man wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) complaining to him of his bereavement with a child of his, and the intensity of what had entered into him. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Do you not know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chooses from the wealth of the Believer and from his children, his most beloved, in order to recompense him upon that'.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah take away the most beloved children or wealth from believers?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of *ikhtiyar* (divine selection), clarifying that Allah does not merely test believers arbitrarily but specifically chooses the most precious of their possessions or children to maximize the spiritual reward for their patience. This perspective shifts the understanding of loss from a punitive measure to a sign of divine favor, encouraging believers to view the removal of beloved entities as an opportunity for elevated status in the Hereafter.
